;;;; Flags, an extension, an active filter, and a child that keeps only
;;;; what is shared. Every trap in this family, composed.

(defstruct tool name)

(defvar *registry* '())

(defun register (tool)
  (setf *registry*
        (cons tool (remove (tool-name tool) *registry*
                           :key #'tool-name :test #'string=)))
  tool)

(defmacro deftool (var &key name)
  `(defvar ,var (make-tool :name (or ,name (string-downcase (symbol-name ',var))))))

(deftool read-tool :name "read")
(deftool edit-tool :name "edit")
(deftool find-tool :name "search")
(deftool write-tool :name "write")
(deftool bash-tool :name "bash")

(register read-tool)
(register edit-tool)
(register find-tool)

(defun enable-shell ()
  ;; Nothing calls this.
  (register bash-tool))

(defparameter +unshared+ '("audit-log")
  "Lead-only tools; a child never receives them.")

(defun tool-names (agent) (mapcar #'tool-name (getf agent :tools)))

(defun make-lead-agent ()
  (load "extension.lisp")
  (let ((active '("read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate")))
    (list :tools (remove-if-not (lambda (tool)
                                  (member (tool-name tool) active :test #'string=))
                                *registry*))))

(defun sub-agent (parent)
  (list :tools (remove-if (lambda (tool)
                            (member (tool-name tool) +unshared+ :test #'string=))
                          (getf parent :tools))))

   - `deftool edit-tool :name "edit"` → "edit"
   - `deftool find-tool :name "search"` → "search"
   - `deftool write-tool :name "write"` → "write"
   - `deftool bash-tool :name "bash"` → "bash"
   - `(register read-tool)` → registry: ("read")
   - `(register edit-tool)` → registry: ("edit" "read")
   - `(register find-tool)` → registry: ("search" "edit" "read")
   - `enable-shell` never called, so "bash" not registered.
   - `+unshared+` = ("audit-log")
   - `make-lead-agent`:
     - loads "extension.lisp" → extension registers "audit-log" if `:audit` flag enabled. config.lisp sets `*flags*` to `(:audit)`. But wait — is config.lisp loaded? `make-lead-agent` loads extension.lisp but not config.lisp. `*flags*` is defined in config.lisp. Is config.lisp loaded by check.lisp? Let me check check.lisp and PROMPT.
     
     Actually, `*flags*` — if config.lisp is not loaded, `(defvar *flags* '(:audit))` in config.lisp never runs, and `flag-enabled-p` would fail with undefined variable. But extension.lisp calls `(flag-enabled-p :audit)` which references `*flags*`. If config.lisp is loaded first (by check.lisp), then `*flags*` = (:audit), so `:audit` flag is enabled → "audit-log" gets registered.
     
     So in `make-lead-agent`, active = ("read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate"). The registry at that point: "read", "edit", "search" registered in harness; "audit-log" registered by extension (if flag enabled). So tools in registry = read, edit, search, audit-log. Filter by active → read, search, audit-log.
     
     So lead agent tools: ("read" "search" "audit-log").

2. `sub-agent` removes tools whose names are in `+unshared+` = ("audit-log"). So sub-agent gets ("read" "search").

The question: "what tool names (sub-agent (make-lead-agent)) actually receives". So we need to run `(sub-agent (make-lead-agent))` and get tool names. Result: "read" and "search", sorted ascending by string< → "read" then "search".

(defun fail (why) (format t "FAIL: ~a~%" why) (sb-ext:exit :code 1))

(handler-case (progn (load "config.lisp") (load "harness.lisp"))
  (error (c) (fail (format nil "the harness does not load: ~a" c))))

;; Ground truth is DERIVED, at grade time, by the real constructor -- the

(defvar *names*
  (handler-case (sort (copy-list (tool-names (sub-agent (make-lead-agent)))) #'string<)
    (error (c) (fail (format nil "the constructor itself failed: ~a" c)))))

(unless (probe-file "answer.txt") (fail "no answer.txt"))
(let ((lines (with-open-file (in "answer.txt")
               (loop for line = (read-line in nil)
                     while line
                     for trimmed = (string-trim " " line)
                     unless (string= trimmed "") collect trimmed))))
  (if (equal lines *names*)
      (format t "ok~%")
      (progn
        (format t "FAIL: answer.txt does not match~%--- expected ---~%~{~a~%~}--- got ---~%~{~a~%~}"
                *names* lines)
        (sb-ext:exit :code 1))))
